transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

For a Panasonic NN-H98 that is not heating, the most common cause is a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit (such as the magnetron, inverter board, or associated components), though it can sometimes be a simple settings issue. This is an engineer-level repair. To confirm whether the microwave function itself has failed (as opposed to just the grill), please do this safe check:
1. Ensure the door is closed firmly and there are no items blocking it from latching.
2. Place a cup of water inside.
3. Set the power level to 100% (Full Power) and start it for one minute.
4. Check if the water is hot. Is the water hot, or still cold?
tried it, stops after 10-15 seconds with H98 and the water is still cold. h98 is what the screen says, model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ

The H98 code combined with the water staying cold and stopping after 10–15 seconds suggests a high-voltage power circuit failure. This specific error almost always points to a fault on the HV Inverter Board or, less commonly, the magnetron itself. This is not safe for a homeowner to repair. The high-voltage capacitor inside can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged, and diagnosing these components requires specialist equipment and safety procedures. Please do not attempt to open the casing or test internal parts yourself. You will need an engineer to replace the faulty component (likely the inverter board). I recommend contacting Panasonic support or a qualified appliance repair technician.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
